title: Lock a trailer door: swing the lock-rod handle in, lift it over the hasp's lip into its seat, flip the keeper down
instruction: Lock this trailer door: swing the lock rod's handle in until it is flat against the door, drop it into its hasp, and flip the hasp's keeper down over it. Then let go.
context: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers (O*NET 53-3032.00; 2,221,200 employed in 2025) "Inspect loads to ensure that cargo is secure." Federal rules bar a driver from moving unless the vehicle's "tailgate, tailboard, doors, tarpaulins, spare tire and other equipment used in its operation, and the means of fastening the commercial motor vehicle's cargo, are secured" (49 CFR 392.9(a)(2)). On a dry van that means the rear doors' cam-action lock rods, worked at every pick-up and delivery. The handle is double-action: turning it turns the rod, whose cam hooks a keeper on the sill and draws the door onto its seal; the handle then has to be lifted over the hasp's lip while it is pushed against the seal's spring-back, let down into the hasp, and trapped there by a flip keeper. A keeper flipped down with the handle not under it looks locked and is not, so that scores zero.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table. A bench section of a dry van's right-hand rear door stands upright on the table, fixed, facing the robot: an 18 mm plywood door panel 49 wide (y -23 to 26) and 28 tall on a 6 x 6 cm sill, its outer face at x 52.0. Left of it, across a 6 mm seam, the edge of the other door (y 26.6 to 44) with its own lock rod at y 33, locked. Lock rod: a 32 cm cut length of 3/4 in Schedule 40 steel pipe (26.7 mm across), upright in two pipe guides, axis at x 48.5, y 19.0, free to turn. At its lower end, 3 cm up, the cam: a steel plate with two prongs 8 mm apart; a 6 mm keeper pin stands on the sill, 3.1 cm from the pipe's axis. Handle: a 14 in (35.6 cm) zinc-plated steel bar, 8 x 25 mm, 0.55 kg, painted red here, pinned to a hub on the pipe 16 cm up so that it turns the rod and can also be lifted up to 30 degrees. Locked, it lies level along the door toward the robot's right, 3.5 cm in front of the door's face. It starts swung out 60 degrees from that toward the robot, its tip at (16.1, 0.3), resting on its hub's stop. Hasp, fixed on the door 30 cm along the locked handle from the pipe (y -11.0): 5-1/8 in tall, 2 in wide; a seat 12 mm deep for the bar, its top 14.7 cm up, with a lip 12 mm high and 5 mm thick in front of it; above the seat, on a pin 22 cm up, the flip keeper, a 28 x 53 x 6 mm steel plate with a 14 mm finger tab, 40 g. The keeper starts flipped up and over, leaning 25 degrees past upright on its stop; flipped down it hangs with its end 2.5 mm above the seated bar. The door's seal pushes back: over the rod's last 15 degrees the handle resists, 2 N at 20 cm from the pipe when flat on the hasp. For real trials the handle, hasp, cam, keeper and pipe guides come from a cam-action door latch kit for 3/4 in pipe (Polar Hardware PLR258-002); the simulated seat, lip, flip keeper, cam and pin are estimates of that kit's parts. Both arms start in their rest pose. Layout B (DOOR_LOT=B): the fixture 1.5 cm further away and 1.5 cm to the right, the handle starting 45 degrees out.
scoring: Scored at the end, from where the parts are then (by eye, a ruler and a feeler). 1.0: the handle is in the hasp's seat (at the hasp, its door-side face within 6 mm of the hasp's face and its underside within 3 mm of the seat, so it is behind the lip), the keeper is down over it (within 10 degrees of hanging), both grippers are at least 3 cm from the handle and the keeper, and nothing is moving. 0.75: handle in its seat and keeper down, but a gripper is within 3 cm or something still moves. 0.5: handle in its seat, keeper not down. 0.25: handle not in its seat and keeper not down, but the cam has hold of its pin (the pin is between the cam's two prongs; the rod within 25 degrees of locked). 0: the keeper is down while the handle is not in its seat (it looks locked and is not), or the cam has no hold. Doing nothing scores 0. A handle swung in and let go outside the hasp is pushed back out by the seal to about 20 degrees, where the cam still has its pin, and scores 0.25.
reset_notes: Flip the keeper up and over onto its stop, lift the handle out of the hasp and swing it out to the start mark (60 degrees; 45 for layout B), resting on its hub's stop. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at full size on three pins (rod in its guides, handle on the hub, keeper on the hasp). Seat, lip, keeper, cam prongs and keeper pin act by contact. One force law stands in for the door seal: a torsion spring on the rod over its last 15 degrees, 0.4 N m at locked (estimate; a real door takes far more). From the kit's listing: 14 in handle, 5-1/8 x 2 in hasp, 3/4 in pipe. Estimates: bar section, masses, seat, lip, keeper, cam and pin shapes, friction. Not tried on a physical rig.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper went to the handle's free end and stayed beside it; the handle was not swung in and the keeper was not touched); demo: 1.0 (the demo video shows the overhead camera beside the right wrist camera)
